purpose: Cefadroxil is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as throat infections (strep throat), skin infections, and urinary tract infections. It works only against bacteria, so it will not help with colds, flu, or other viral illnesses. Your doctor prescribed it to help your body fight off a specific bacterial infection.
how_it_works: Cefadroxil works by attacking the outer wall that surrounds bacteria. Think of the bacterial wall like a protective shell — cefadroxil damages that shell so the bacteria fall apart and die. Without that wall, the bacteria cannot survive, and your infection clears up.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are stomach upset, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. Taking it with food can help reduce stomach issues. Some people may notice a mild skin rash. These effects are usually not serious and often go away on their own.
warnings: Tell your doctor right away if you develop a severe rash, hives, swelling of your face or throat, or trouble breathing, as these could be signs of a serious allergic reaction. Let your doctor know if you are allergic to penicillin, since there is a small chance of a related reaction. If you develop severe or persistent diarrhea, contact your doctor, as it could be a sign of a gut infection. Always finish the full course of antibiotics even if you feel better early.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 1,000 to 2,000 mg per day, taken either as one dose or split into two doses, depending on your infection. For children, the dose is based on their weight. It can be taken with or without food, but taking it with food helps if it upsets your stomach. Always follow your doctor's or pharmacist's specific instructions.
